studies.title: Intrinsic capacity with COVID-19 infection and late complications in the older adult population.
studies.authors: Nikbakht, Hossein-Ali, Bakhtiari, Afsaneh, Tamadoni, Negar, Sivan, Manoj et al.
studies.abstract: Intrinsic capacity (IC) decline, infection susceptibility, and post-COVID sequelae in older adults, intensified by the pandemic, demand probing IC domains' infection/outcome links and population-level strategies for sustaining functional health. This cross-sectional study enrolled 600 older adults. IC was assessed using the World Health Organization's ICOPE framework. Post-COVID-19 condition was defined according to Centers for Disease Control and Prevention criteria, and late complications were evaluated via the culturally adapted and validated Persian C19-YRS questionnaire. COVID-19 infection status was confirmed through polymerase chain reaction testing of nasopharyngeal swabs or serological antibody assays. Statistical analyses were conducted using SPSS Version 22, including independent t-tests, analysis of variance, and regression models. Overall, most participants demonstrated relatively preserved IC across domains, although greater variability was observed in the psychological domain. In multivariable analysis, higher scores in the psychological IC domain were independently associated with COVID-19 infection (OR = 1.04, 95% CI: 1.00-1.08). Lower cognitive and sensory IC scores were significantly associated with poorer functional ability (B = -0.35, 95% CI: -0.66 to -0.04; and B = -0.50, 95% CI: -0.90 to -0.10, respectively), while higher sensory IC scores were associated with better general health among participants with post-COVID-19 complications (B = 0.24, 95% CI: 0.01-0.47). These findings indicate meaningful associations between IC and both COVID-19 infection status and post-infectious health outcomes in older adults. Monitoring and supporting IC may be relevant for maintaining functional independence and quality of life in ageing populations during and after widespread infectious disease outbreaks.

The syphilis in pregnancy detection rate increased until 2018 and remained stable thereafter. Changes in clinical and epidemiological characteristics reflect variations in the care context, with advances in prenatal care, but persistence of weaknesses in the timely diagnosis and treatment of partners. studies.title: Strong Protein Responses to Acute Infection Control General Post-Viral Sequelae and SARS-CoV-2-specific Neurocognitive Sequelae.
studies.journal: medRxiv : the preprint server for health sciences
studies.authors: Liou, Theodore G, Andrews, Ryan J, Battey, Heather S, Bass, Brenda L et al.
studies.abstract: After serious infections, many survivors fully recover while others face persistent symptoms including neurocognitive dysfunction, cardiopulmonary instabilities and disabling fatigue, classified broadly as Post-Acute Infection Syndromes (PAIS). Post-Acute Sequelae of COVID19 (PASC) is one special case. To test whether acute infection initiates PAIS, we analyzed proteins in 173 saliva samples collected during severe respiratory viral infections and tracked patient outcomes for five years. We discovered 44 proteins, all derived from interferon stimulated genes, that respond strongly to acute infection. Rates of post-acute syndromes were similar regardless of infection, but the types of Sequelae differed by virus. High expression of 19 proteins predict low General Sequelae rates across all viruses. High expression of 23 overlapping proteins predict low Neurocognitive Sequelae rates only with SARS-CoV-2 infections. We propose that low expressions of these proteins, which control viral replication, innate immunity, and secondary autoimmunity, combine to precipitate PAIS and PASC. Acute viral infections elicit interferon stimulated gene (ISG) protein responses.23 ISG proteins prevent post-infection General Sequelae for all viral infections.19 ISG proteins prevent post-infection Neurocognitive Sequelae only with SARS-CoV-2.Poor protein responses induce distinct post-viral syndromes with or without COVID19.

studies.title: Prevalence and Trends of Post-COVID-19 Sequelae Among U.S. Adults With Prior COVID-19 Infection, 2022-2024.
studies.authors: Bhargava, Ashish, Szpunar, Susan
studies.abstract: Post-acute sequelae of SARS-CoV-2 infection (PASC) affect a substantial proportion of U.S. adults, involving multiple organ systems and resulting in significant disability and diminished quality of life. Population-level PASC estimates include individuals without prior COVID-19 infection and therefore do not accurately reflect postinfection risk required for effective risk stratification. We estimated the prevalence and trends of PASC among U.S. adults with prior COVID-19. We analyzed data from the National Health Interview Survey (2022-2024), a nationally representative survey of the U.S. civilian noninstitutionalized population. Adults reporting prior COVID-19 infection were asked whether they ever experienced symptoms lasting ≥3 months that were not present before infection; those answering yes were classified as having PASC. Weighted analyses accounted for the complex survey design. Among 42,872 adults with prior COVID-19, 6,822 reported symptoms lasting three months or longer, indicating PASC. Prevalence declined from 19.7% in 2022 to 15.1% in 2023 and 13.7% in 2024 (P<0.001 for 2022 vs subsequent years). Despite this decline, more than 21 million U.S. adults reported having experienced PASC in 2023 and 2024. Prevalence was higher among women and adults aged 35-64 years than among men and younger or elderly individuals. A lower prevalence was observed among Asian adults, whereas a higher prevalence was noted among American Indian, Alaska Native, and multiracial adults. Despite declining prevalence, PASC remains common among U.S. adults with prior COVID-19. These nationally representative postinfection estimates provide clinically relevant risk information to guide patient counseling, health system planning, and ongoing surveillance.

studies.title: Economic Burden of Post-COVID Syndrome in Germany Between 2021 and 2025: A Statutory Health Insurance Claims Data Analysis.
studies.journal: Journal of health economics and outcomes research
studies.authors: Gensorowsky, Daniel, Fröling, Emma, Braegelmann, Kylie, Diekmannshemke, Jana et al.
studies.abstract: Evidence on the economic burden of post-COVID syndrome in Germany remains limited. This study quantifies post-COVID-associated healthcare resource utilization (HCRU), sick leave, and costs. To compare HCRU, sick leave, and costs borne by the statutory health insurance (SHI) among incident pediatric and adult post-COVID patients with matched post-COVID-free controls. This retrospective cohort study analyzed an anonymized German SHI claims database provided by GWQ ServicePlus AG. The observation period spanned October 2021 to June 2025 and included all individuals with incident COVID-19 diagnosis until September 2024. Incident post-COVID was defined as the first ICD-10-GM code (U07.4!; U09.9!) recorded ≥90 days after first COVID-19 diagnosis. Post-COVID cases were exactly matched 1:2 to post-COVID-free COVID-19 controls by calendar quarter of incident COVID-19 diagnosis, acute severity, cohort entry quarter, 5-year birth interval, sex, and Elixhauser Comorbidity Index. We estimated mean differences in HCRU, sick leave, and direct SHI-borne costs per case. Rate ratios of HCRU, sick leave, and costs per person-year were estimated using Poisson (HCRU/sick leave) and linear (costs) regression. Analyses covered 365-day, 730-day, and any follow-up period. We matched 25 485 identified post-COVID cases with 49 671 controls. Matched cases and controls were comparable in age, sex, and comorbidities. Overall, during 365 days of follow-up, post-COVID patients showed higher HCRU and sick leave rates across all sectors, especially sick leave days. Mean differences per case were greatest for sick leave days (365 days: +27 days) and outpatient physician contacts (365 days: 6.9 contacts). HCRU and sick leave rates remained significantly increased over extended follow-up periods. Total SHI-borne costs per person-year were higher among post-COVID patients across all follow-up periods (all Documented post-COVID was associated with a substantial and sustained economic burden on the German healthcare system and society. Targeted strategies are needed to mitigate potential long-term impacts on HCRU and labor productivity.

studies.title: Multifactorial biomarker profiles in fatigued and non-fatigued post-COVID-19 patients: insights from a one-year follow-up.
studies.authors: Barrero-Santiago, Laura, Gomes de Jesus Ferreira, Leandro, Salomão, Rebecca, da Silva Almeida, Isabella et al.
studies.abstract: To compare blood biomarkers across SARS-CoV-2 fatigue, non-fatigue, and control groups; assessed longitudinal biomarker changes; and identified genetic associations and biomarkers linked to post-COVID-19 fatigue. This longitudinal observational study followed individuals with confirmed SARS-CoV-2 infection over a one-year period, stratifying them into fatigue (n = 27) and non-fatigue (n = 13) groups based on the Fatigue Severity Scale (FSS). These groups were cross-sectionally compared with a non-infected control cohort (n = 27). Blood samples were collected at four time points to assess cytokines, hematological and biochemical markers, inflammatory indices, and matrix metalloproteinases. Selected functional polymorphisms were genotyped using PCR-RFLP. Group comparisons were conducted using generalized estimating equations, and genetic associations were evaluated using odds ratios and 95% confidence intervals. At baseline, fatigued post-COVID participants had higher IL-6 (2.70 vs. 1.68 pg/mL, p < 0.001), IL-8 (6.09 vs. 3.68 pg/mL, p = 0.024), and hs-CRP (6.61 vs. 1.06 mg/L, p < 0.001) than controls. Across follow-up, the fatigued group showed higher IL-6 (mean difference [MD] 1.27 pg/mL, p = 0.009), IL-8 (MD 1.98 pg/mL, p = 0.017), and hs-CRP (MD 4.16 mg/L, p < 0.001) than the non-fatigued group. In exploratory genotype analyses, fatigue was associated with COMT rs4680 (OR 13.85, 95% CI 2.74-69.91), NR3C1 rs41423247 (OR 3.76, 95% CI 1.04-13.69), and MMP9 rs3918242 (OR 0.20, 95% CI 0.06-0.67). Hs-CRP was significantly associated with FSS score (B = 0.12, 95% CI 0.02-0.21; p = 0.014). Post-COVID fatigue was associated with persistent inflammation and genetic variation, supporting a multifactorial biological basis and highlighting hs-CRP as a potential marker requiring further validation.

studies.title: Post-COVID syndrome's impact on sex life - results from a cross-sectional study.
studies.authors: Schröder, Dominik, Schmachtenberg, Tim, Heinemann, Stephanie, Müllenmeister, Christina et al.
studies.abstract: Having a satisfying sexual life is important to many people and impairment of sexual function is often perceived as a burden. This study investigates the self-perceived impairments to sex life in adults with Post-COVID-19 syndrome (PCS) and factors that are associated with impaired sex life. A cross-sectional online survey of people with PCS and without PCS was conducted in Northern Germany. Sex life impairments were assessed using item 8 (frequency and quality of sex life) of the Index for the Assessment of Health Impairments (IMET), scored from 0 (no impairment) to 10 (no activity possible). Scores were analyzed as a continuous outcome because no validated cut-offs have been established for this individual item. Linear regression models were used to adjust for sociodemographic factors as well as medical and mental health conditions. Sample weighting for age and gender was applied in sensitivity analyses to adjust for a representative sample of people with PCS. A total of 892 participants were included, with 67.8% (n = 605) reporting PCS. Persons with PCS reported significantly higher sex life impairments (mean score 4.62) compared to those without PCS (mean score 2.58, p < 0.001). The regression model confirmed that PCS was associated with sex life impairments (β = 1.16, p < 0.001). No significant correlation was found between sex life impairments and the symptom duration symptoms or the respondents´ gender. Impaired sex life is a significant concern for PCS patients, that warrants attention from healthcare providers. Our findings highlight the importance of addressing sex life impairments in the care of people with PCS.

studies.title: Scavenger Receptor Class B Type 1 Mediated Transport Enables Delivery Across Capillarized Liver Sinusoids in Metabolic Dysfunction-Associated Steatohepatitis.
studies.authors: Yuan, Ruyan, Zhang, Jiamin, Huang, Yamei, Meng, Yiyang et al.
studies.abstract: Liver fibrosis in metabolic dysfunction associated steatohepatitis (MASH) lacks effective therapies, in part because therapeutic agents poorly penetrate the capillarized sinusoidal endothelium. As fibrosis progresses, liver sinusoidal endothelial cells (LSECs) become defenestrated and restrict trans-sinusoidal exchange, thereby limiting drug access to hepatic stellate cells (HSCs) within the perisinusoidal space. Here, we developed a lipoprotein mimetic liposomal nanocarrier, SV@SRB-Lip, to exploit scavenger receptor class B type 1 (SR-B1)-associated transendothelial transport across capillarized LSECs and enhance downstream delivery toward HSC-associated fibrotic regions. SV@SRB-Lip was engineered as a simvastatin loaded liposomal platform incorporating an ApoA-I-mimetic SRB peptide, an MMP-responsive linker, and a vitamin A modified lipid moiety. SV@SRB-Lip promoted transport across the LSEC monolayer in vitro, and this effect was reduced by SR-B1 silencing, supporting the involvement of SR-B1-associated endothelial transport. In MASH mice, SV@SRB-Lip enhanced hepatic delivery and distributed toward HSC associated fibrotic regions. The MMP-responsive design increased the relative accessibility of vitamin A within the fibrotic microenvironment, supporting downstream HSC associated uptake. As a result, SV@SRB-Lip increased hepatic simvastatin accumulation, suppressed HSC activation and collagen deposition, and improved MASH associated fibrosis. These findings suggest that SR-B1-associated endothelial transport can be harnessed to overcome the capillarized sinusoidal barrier and improve antifibrotic nanomedicine delivery in MASH.

studies.title: Central Nervous System Alterations in Individuals with Long COVID: A Systematic Review.
studies.journal: Revista da Sociedade Brasileira de Medicina Tropical
studies.authors: Moraes, Janaina Ferreira de, Souza, Paulo Henrique Leite, Andrade, Michele Lacerda de, Dias, Raphael Mendes Ritti et al.
studies.abstract: Long COVID (post-COVID-19 condition) has been associated with persistent neurological and cognitive symptoms, suggesting possible central nervous system involvement beyond the acute phase of severe acute respiratory syndrome coronavirus 2 infection. A systematic review of articles published up to April 2026 was conducted following the PRISMA guidelines, and observational studies evaluating neurophysiological, structural, and functional alterations in individuals with long COVID were analyzed. Forty-two studies with substantial variability in design and methods were included; thus, the findings were synthesized narratively. The evidence indicates heterogeneous yet recurrent alterations in the central nervous system of individuals with lonf COVID, including impaired cortical excitability, abnormal cerebral oscillatory activity across multiple frequency bands, changes in functional connectivity, and structural abnormalities in neural networks. Some studies also reported imbalances in excitatory-inhibitory neurotransmission and biomarkers suggestive of neuroinflammation or axonal injury. These neurophysiological and structural alterations were commonly associated with persistent fatigue, cognitive dysfunction, and brain fog. However, the available evidence is limited by important methodological issues, including substantial heterogeneity in study populations, assessment techniques, and reported outcomes; the observational design also limited the strength of the conclusions. Taken together, the current evidence suggests a persistent and multifactorial central nervous system dysfunction in long COVID. However, definitive conclusions remain limited, and well-designed prospective longitudinal studies using standardized methods are needed to clarify the mechanisms, duration, and clinical relevance of these alterations.

studies.title: Prevalence of alpha-synuclein seeding activity in the Olfactory Mucosa following SARS-CoV-2 infection: results from a pilot study.
studies.authors: Heim, Beatrice, Seppi, Klaus, De Cleene, Nicolas, Bongianni, Matilde et al.
studies.abstract: Olfactory dysfunction (OD) is a hallmark of SARS-CoV-2-infection where it is believed to result from neuroinflammation induced by viral invasion via the olfactory mucosa (OM). Hyposmia also affects the majority of patients with Parkinson's disease (PD) where it is caused by α-synuclein (aSyn) pathology in the olfactory system, and aSyn-seeding-activity can be detected in the OM using aSyn-seeding-amplification-assays (aSyn-SAA). The present pilot study aimed to investigate whether SARS-CoV-2-infection induces local aSyn-misfolding and -aggregation in OM samples using aSyn-SAA. We conducted an observational study including PD patients (n = 51), individuals with a history of documented symptomatic SARS-CoV-2-infection (post-COVID; n = 95), and healthy controls (HC; n = 42). Post-COVID-participants were stratified based on persistent OD (COVID+OD; n = 42) or normal olfaction (COVID-OD; n = 53) using Sniffin'-Sticks-Identification (SSI) and -Discrimination (SSD) tests. OM samples were obtained by ENT specialists and analyzed by aSyn-SAA at the University of Verona. Clinical phenotyping included MDS-UPDRS, MoCA, and the Innsbruck-RBD-Inventory. OM-SAA positivity rates were significantly different between PD and both post-COVID-participants and HCs (80.4% vs 24.2% vs 11.9%; p < 0.001). Within the post-COVID-group, positivity rates were higher in COVID+OD vs COVID-OD (35.7% vs 15.1%; p = 0.030), and COVID+OD differed from HC (p = 0.030), while COVID-OD did not (p = 0.65). Among post-COVID-participants, aSyn-SAA positivity was associated with lower SSI (p = 0.007) and SSD (p < 0.001) scores, but not with MDS-UPDRS, MoCA, or RBD measures. OM-SAA-positivity was enriched among individuals with persistent post-COVID-OD and correlated with olfactory impairment. These findings support the hypothesis that neuroinflammation following SARS-COV-2-infection might promote local aSyn-aggregation. The biological and prognostic relevance of OM-SAA positivity is unknown and needs further prospective investigation.

studies.title: A narrative review of stem cell-based therapy for fibrosing interstitial lung diseases: clinical evidence and translational perspectives.
studies.authors: Li, Zhengnan, Geng, Lei, Li, Wei, Wang, Xiujuan et al.
studies.abstract: Fibrosing interstitial lung diseases (F-ILD) are a heterogeneous group of disorders characterized by pulmonary interstitial fibrosis and inflammation. Idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis (IPF) is the most common and severe form of F-ILD. Regulator-approved anti-fibrotic drugs, such as pirfenidone and nintedanib, delay rather than reverse disease progression, so the threat of eventual respiratory failure remains. While lung transplantation is an option that can prolong survival for end-stage IPF, its clinical application is greatly restricted by donor shortages, surgical risks, and postoperative complications. Stem cell therapies, and particularly treatments based on mesenchymal stromal/stem cells (MSCs) and their derivatives, have brought new hope for the management of F-ILD due to their immune regulatory, anti-inflammatory, and anti-fibrotic capabilities. A search was conducted to identify relevant articles in the PubMed/MEDLINE, Web of Science, Cochrane Library, China National Knowledge Internet and Wanfang Data from inception to 31st May 2026. This review summarizes the mechanistic overview of stem cell-based therapeutic strategies for F-ILD, safety profiles and therapeutic potentials of various stem cells for the treatment of IPF and other F-ILDs, with an emphasis on stem cell types and delivery routine. This article also discusses the challenges and limitations of stem cell-based therapies, highlighting the need for further clinical studies with standardized efficacy endpoints to validate their effectiveness.

studies.title: Long COVID is associated with lipoxygenase-catalyzed metabolism of essential polyunsaturated fatty acids.
studies.authors: Moss, M Elizabeth, Pons, Stephanie, Tavares, Luciana P, Tang, Yan et al.
studies.abstract: Long COVID (LC) represents a failure of healthy resolution mechanisms for inflammation after SARS-CoV-2 infection. Dietary essential polyunsaturated fatty acids (PUFAs) and their downstream metabolites can orchestrate inflammation resolution, suggesting these pathways may be altered in LC. In this study, plasma samples from two independent participant cohorts totaling 106 participants (designated by chart review as LC or Recovered) were collected longitudinally in the 12 months following SARS-CoV-2 infection and analyzed by mass spectrometry for targeted PUFA metabolites. In the acute phase of SARS-CoV-2 infection, upregulation of PUFA metabolites downstream of 12-lipoxygenase was associated with later development of LC. In the months following infection, LC participants displayed uncoupling of PUFA-related lipid metabolism and altered lipoxygenase-driven metabolism over time compared to recovered participants. These results provide new mechanistic insights for the development of LC and suggest potential therapeutic strategies for this prevalent and debilitating disorder.

studies.title: Test-retest reliability and interpretability of Long COVID Burden Index: A prospective observational study.
studies.journal: Journal of infection and chemotherapy : official journal of the Japan Society of Chemotherapy
studies.authors: Yamada, Gen, Iwamoto, Noriko, Miyamori, Daisuke, Suzuki, Michiyo et al.
studies.abstract: The Long COVID Burden Index (LCBI) is an 11-item patient-reported outcome measure developed to assess the burden of long COVID symptoms on daily life. Although its cross-sectional validity and internal consistency have been demonstrated, its test-retest reliability, measurement error, and minimal important change (MIC) have not yet been evaluated. We conducted a longitudinal postal survey among adults with a history of COVID-19 hospitalization. The LCBI was administered at the initial survey, 2-week follow-up, and 3-month follow-up. Test-retest reliability was assessed among participants who completed the initial and 2-week surveys and reported no change on a 7-point global rating of change question. Measurement error was evaluated using the standard error of measurement (SEM) and the smallest detectable change (SDC) was calculated. The MIC was estimated at 3 months by using anchor-based methods: the mean change method, receiver operating characteristic curve analysis, and predictive modeling. Among 1031 potential participants, 301 provided valid responses at the initial survey, 258 at the 2-week follow-up, and 208 at the 3-months follow-up. The intraclass correlation coefficient for the LCBI total score was 0.78 (95% confidence interval, 0.72-0.83). The SEM and SDC were 3.26 and 9.04 points, respectively. The MIC estimates ranged from 1.73 to 2.91 points across methods. The LCBI showed good test-retest reliability. A reduction of approximately 2-3 points may represent a minimal important improvement. However, this change is below the SDC and does not provide definitive evidence of change beyond measurement error.

studies.title: Protective Effect of COVID-19 Vaccination on Post-Infection Visuospatial Deficits.
studies.journal: Revista brasileira de psiquiatria (Sao Paulo, Brazil : 1999)
studies.authors: da Silva, Lucas Gomes, Fini, Bruna Carmeni Di, Oliveira, Jordano César Milagres, Rosa, Daniela Valadão et al.
studies.abstract: COVID-19 has been associated with persistent cognitive deficits months after SARS-CoV-2 infection. Vaccination reduces severe disease, but its effect on post-infection cognition remains uncertain. We evaluated whether COVID-19 vaccination attenuates cognitive deficits after SARS-CoV-2. We assessed 237 adults with COVID-19 and 105 controls. Patients were grouped by vaccination status at infection (vaccinated n=87; unvaccinated n=150). The neuropsychological assessment covered language, visuospatial ability, visual memory, verbal memory, attention, executive functions, and working memory. Group differences were tested with Aligned Rank Transform ANOVA with Holm-corrected post hoc comparisons, adjusting for education. Significant group differences were observed in visuospatial ability and visual memory, assessed with the Rey-Osterrieth Complex Figure Test (Copy, Immediate and Delayed Recall) (all p < 0.001). The vaccinated group outperformed the unvaccinated group (p = 0.022) on visuospatial performance. The Rey-Osterrieth Complex Figure Test Copy did not differ significantly among participants vaccinated with CoronaVac, AstraZeneca, or Pfizer. The findings suggest that COVID-19 vaccination may mitigate post-infection visuospatial deficits, reinforcing the importance of immunization in preventing cognitive sequelae associated with the disease.

studies.title: Blood biomarkers of long COVID: A cross-sectional evaluation of key cytokines and the coordination of inflammation.
studies.authors: Thomas, Callum, Ashton, Ruth E, Pretorius, Etheresia, Owen, Rebecca et al.
studies.abstract: Long COVID is a complex pathophysiological condition linked to a heterogenous symptom profile. Dysregulation of 1) immunological and inflammatory responses, 2) endothelial/vascular function, and 3) metabolic and clotting processes have been identified; however, there remains a lack of clinically validated diagnostic biomarkers. The study aim was to investigate dysregulation of cytokines, chemokines and growth factors in confirmed Long COVID cases grouped by disease severity. One-hundred-and-twenty-seven participants provided venous blood samples for cytokine profiling utilising Luminex assays. Participants were grouped into those with no knowledge of SARS-CoV-2 infection (n = 21), acute infection within 3-months (n = 22), spontaneous resolvers (>3-months, n = 21) and those with confirmed Long COVID (n = 63). Long COVID severity was grouped according to the post-COVID-19 functional status (PCFS) and defined as those with negligible (4A; n = 9), mild (4B; n = 20), moderate (4C; n = 24), and severe limitations (4D; n = 10). Cytokines were assessed for normality using Shapiro-Wilk tests and differences measured between groups using Kruskal-Wallis tests. Pairwise correlation and principal component analysis were performed. Interleukin-12 (p40/p70) was 22% greater in the Long COVID group (Median [IQR]: 58 [49] pg/mL, p = 0.046) and 30% greater in the acutely infected group (64 [36] pg/mL; p = 0.039) against non-infected controls (45 [25] pg/mL). Following PCFS classification, fibroblast growth factor-basic was 25% lower in Long COVID 4B versus spontaneous resolvers (24 [7] vs. 32 [24] pg/mL; p = 0.025). Pairwise correlation differences demonstrated that three Long COVID subgroups had strong, positive associations between cytokines when compared to non-infected controls; however, PCA was unable to determine any coordinated cytokine variation that was group specific. Elevated interleukin-12 (p40/p70) and reduced basic fibroblast growth factor suggest persistent immune activation and possible subgroup-specific Long COVID; however, these findings were marginally significant and exploratory. A coordinated but partial immunological/inflammatory profile may exist in some of those with Long COVID, suggesting a rationale for subgrouping upon a biological, rather than self-report basis but larger longitudinal studies are required to confirm this hypothesis.

studies.title: Evaluating the Mental Fatigue Scale for long COVID: A content validity study.
studies.authors: Riis-Djernæs, Line M, Oestergaard, Lisa Gregersen, Nielsen, Trine Brøns, Sørensen, Lotte et al.
studies.abstract: This study aimed to evaluate the content validity of the Mental Fatigue Scale (MFS) in individuals with long COVID. Content validity was assessed using COSMIN methodology through cognitive interviews with individuals with long COVID (n = 10) and focus groups with healthcare professionals (n = 8). The interviews were conducted at a Danish long COVID clinic and a community-based rehabilitation centre. MFS was generally perceived as relevant, comprehensive, and comprehensible for assessing mental fatigue in individuals with long COVID. Most participants found the items appropriate; however, some described experiences, such as word-finding difficulties and racing thoughts, not fully captured by the scale. Participants also compared symptoms to their pre COVID condition rather than to the previous month, suggesting that the timeframe may require adjustment. Several noted that the MFS reflects symptoms at the body-function level and offers limited insight into how mental fatigue affects participation in work, social, and family life. The MFS appears useful for assessing mental fatigue in individuals with long COVID but may benefit from supplementary items relevant to this population or from being combined with tools that capture broader participation-related and contextual factors. Future studies should adapt and evaluate the scale in this population.

studies.title: Effects of prolonged SARS-CoV2 spike protein exposure in long COVID and a mouse model of the disease.
studies.authors: Nuovo, Gerard, Laurence, Jeffrey, Tili, Esmerina, Li, Xing et al.
studies.abstract: We addressed the question: can the SARS-CoV2 spike protein persist in ACE2+ endothelia in the CNS/other sites and induce a prolonged microvasculature injury syndrome? People who died from COVID-19, with age-matched controls, and people with long COVID with symptoms persisting from 1-5 years, with controls of people who had recovered from COVID-19, were studied. Also compared were WT mice injected with the spike protein sacrificed at day 5 versus 1.5 months. The ACE2+ microvasculature density in the CNS increased 19-fold in the mice exposed to spike for 1.5 months. Human fatal COVID-19 cases showed an ACE2+ CNS density of 13.2/3.9 versus 2.1/0.9 for the controls. Long Covid cases showed an ACE2 microvasculature density of 11.9/3.0 versus 3.5/0.9 for the people who recovered from COVID (each p value < 0.001). Viral spike microvasculature density in the CNS was similar in the fatal COVID-19 cases (6.9/2.1) and mice (7.0/4.0) and in the skin of long-COVID cases (6.0/1.9) and less in people who recovered from COVID-19 (0.9/0.3) (each p < 0.001). Microvasculature collagen 1 deposition was only evident in fatal COVID, long COVID, and in the mice exposed to S1 for 1.5 mo. Thus, SARS-CoV2 spike (S1) protein can persist for months/years with an associated microvasculature pro-inflammatory state and a restrictive fibrosing microangiopathy; and exposure to high dose S1 markedly increases ACE2 endothelial density.

studies.title: Resilience as social practice: Negotiating long COVID at the intersection of illness and ageing.
studies.authors: Fang, Chao, Comery, Alastair, Baz, Sarah Akhtar, Sheard, Laura et al.
studies.abstract: Resilience is often framed within neoliberal health discourses as an individual capacity for adaptation, obscuring how the ability to endure illness is socially organised. This article reconceptualises resilience as a biographically embedded social practice through a study of older and emerging older adults living with Long COVID, an uncertain chronic health condition that unsettles everyday life and expectations of ageing. Drawing on longitudinal qualitative data from a UK study comprising three phases of 23 interviews (2021-2023), this article presents four illustrative cases of participants aged over 50. Rather than a static attribute, resilience was a dynamic and often painful process in which participants situated the present in relation to past experiences and (un)imagined futures, while seeking to maintain a coherent sense of self amid disruption. This work was enacted through everyday practices such as adjusting routines, renegotiating roles and seeking recognition in healthcare and social relationships. These efforts were enabled or constrained by social conditions, including institutional acknowledgement, material resources and normative expectations of ageing, sometimes leading resilience to be performed rather than authentically experienced. A central finding is that resilience involved learning to live with ambiguity. An uncertain prognosis disrupted biographical continuity and required continual recalibration of temporal horizons, often producing experiences of accelerated or disjunct ageing. Resilience therefore emerged not as recovery but as the socially mediated maintenance of a liveable biography. Recognising resilience as social practice foregrounds the need to reorganise the institutional and relational conditions that make endurance possible.

studies.title: [Recognizing and managing post-exertional malaise in primary care].
studies.authors: Garcia, Sara, Tzartzas, Konstantinos, von Plessen, Christian, Favrat, Bernard et al.
studies.abstract: Post-exertional malaise (PEM) is a syndrome characterized by a worsening of symptoms after physical, cognitive, or emotional exertion. It presents as increased fatigue, usually accompanied by other clinical symptoms, such as muscle pain or cognitive impairment. First described in patients with chronic fatigue syndrome/myalgic encephalomyelitis (CFS/ME), PEM is now recognized as a hallmark of post-infectious syndromes that have received increasing attention through the emergence of long COVID. PEM is a distinguishing symptom of these conditions, and its early detection and appropriate management are essential to prevent long-term functional decline of affected patients. This review describes the definition and clinical impact of PEM and summarizes current recommendations for its management. Le malaise post-effort (MPE) est un syndrome d’aggravation de symptômes à la suite d’un effort physique, cognitif, social ou émotionnel. Il se manifeste par une péjoration de la fatigue associée à d’autres symptômes, comme des douleurs musculaires ou des troubles cognitifs. Initialement décrit chez les personnes atteintes du syndrome de fatigue chronique/encéphalomyélite myalgique (SFC/EM), le MPE se retrouve également dans les syndromes postinfectieux mis en lumière par l’émergence du Covid long. La détection précoce du MPE, symptôme discriminant de ces pathologies, et sa prise en charge adéquate sont fondamentales afin d’améliorer le pronostic et d’éviter la détérioration de l’état fonctionnel des patients concernés. Cet article vise à détailler la définition, l’impact clinique et les stratégies de gestion du MPE.

studies.title: Post-COVID-19 Condition has High Prevalence in Patients with Immune-mediated Inflammatory Diseases and Negatively Impacts Quality of Life.
studies.authors: Schlosser, Tobias, Krasselt, Marco, Hecker, Martin, Holler, Babett et al.
studies.abstract: Pandemic situation by severe acute respiratory syndrome coronavirus 2 and the associated disease (coronavirus disease 2019 [COVID-19]) presents broad challenges. Post-COVID-19 condition represents a continuum of persistent symptoms following the acute course. The World Health Organization (WHO) proposes a definition with at least one symptom persisting for 3 months postonset. Negative affection toward quality of life (QoL) is frequently reported. Patients with immune-mediated inflammatory diseases (IMIDs), such as inflammatory bowel disease (IBD) and rheumatic diseases (RDs) are of scientific interest as immunologic factors and immunosuppressive therapy might influence QoL in post-COVID-19 conditions. Adult IMID patients (≥18 years) were offered participation in this study at our university outpatient center. Data collection was questionnaire-based and recorded individual COVID-19 history and persisting symptoms. QoL has been assessed by several standardized and validated patient-reported outcome measures (Short IBD Questionnaire and Patient Health Questionnaire 4, 5Q-5D-5L). A total of 156 patients were included (117 [75%] with IBD, 39 [25%] with RDs). Eighty-one patients (51%) reported a positive COVID-19 history, mostly with mild courses. Only two (2%) required hospitalization, one requiring intensive care. Seven (9%) reported no symptoms, while 20 (25%) met the WHO criterion for post-COVID-19 condition; 19 (23%) were still suffering from post-COVID-19 at the time of data acquisition. Mean/median global QoL scores (scale from 0 [=lowest] to 100 [=highest]) were 71.5/75 in patients without post-COVID-19, compared to 61.9/60 in those with the condition. A one-sided A relevant fraction of IMID patients suffered from post-COVID-19 condition. This condition negatively impacted the individual QoL.

studies.title: Post-translational modifications in the insoluble fraction of platelet-poor plasma distinguish pre-COVID-19 Postural Orthostatic Tachycardia Syndrome, Long COVID, and Long COVID-POTS: a preliminary study.
studies.authors: Booyens, Renata M, Vlok, Mare, Bester, Cecile, Hira, Rashmin et al.
studies.abstract: Pre-COVID-19 Postural Orthostatic Tachycardia Syndrome (PC-POTS), Long COVID with initial orthostatic hypotension (LC-IOH), and Long COVID-POTS (LC-POTS) are primarily chronic post-viral conditions with debilitating symptoms, despite routine laboratory findings often being normal. We previously identified amyloidogenic fibrinaloid microclot complexes (FMCs) in the insoluble fraction of platelet-poor plasma (PPP-IF) in Long COVID, but it remains unclear whether similar abnormalities occur in PC-POTS and LC-POTS, or whether post-translational modifications (PTMs) contribute to disease mechanisms. Platelet-poor plasma from healthy controls (n = 18), PC-POTS (n = 20), LC-IOH (n = 19), and LC-POTS (n = 18) participants underwent proteomic analysis of the PPP-IF using double trypsin digestion and data-independent LC-MS/MS. Differential protein abundance, PTMs, and amyloidogenicity were compared across groups. Although few proteins were significantly dysregulated, extensive disease-specific PTM alterations were identified across coagulation, immune, and metabolic pathways. LC-IOH demonstrated prominent AGE- and oxidation-related PTMs on fibrinogen subunits, particularly fibrinogen alpha chain (FIBA), resembling diabetic glycation profiles. PC-POTS showed fewer fibrinogen PTMs but marked metabolic and immune dysregulation, including oxidised apoA1 and apoB and complement-associated proteins (C3, C4A/B, IC1), IGG1, and A2MG. LC-POTS shared coagulation-related features with LC-IOH and immune-related features with PC-POTS. Many dysregulated peptides were highly amyloidogenic in silico, consistent with β-sheet-rich FMCs. PTM dysregulation was substantially greater than protein-level changes. This study provides the first evidence that PTMs within the PPP-IF has the potential to distinctly differentiate PC-POTS, LC-IOH, and LC-POTS. Because PC-POTS samples predated SARS-CoV-2, their PTM signatures reflect intrinsic disease biology independent of COVID-19. PTM profiling revealed pro-coagulant fibrinogen changes in LC-IOH and LC-POTS, metabolic-oxidative dysregulation in LC-IOH and PC-POTS, and immune dysregulation in PC-POTS and LC-POTS. These abnormalities were not detectable by routine assays and may contribute to microvascular dysfunction. The findings support disease-specific biomarker development and targeted therapeutic strategies across autonomic and post-viral disorders.

studies.title: Obstructive sleep apnea is frequent in patients with Long COVID fatigue but is not significantly associated with alterations of quality of life and cognition.
studies.authors: Bawa, Aasheeta P, Lopez, Melissa, Miller, Janet, Sala, Marc A et al.
studies.abstract: Neurologic manifestations of Long COVID, also called post-acute sequelae of SARS-CoV-2 infection (PASC), include fatigue, cognitive dysfunction, sleep disturbances, and headaches, which can be debilitating. Since these symptoms overlap with those of obstructive sleep apnea (OSA), we sought to determine the prevalence of OSA in the population of a Neuro-COVID-19 clinic. We performed home sleep testing in 100 consecutive patients with Long COVID and no prior history of OSA who reported fatigue after an episode of COVID-19 not requiring hospitalization. The average age was 46.4 years and 70% of patients were female. OSA was present in 53% of patients, including 33% with mild OSA (apnea-hypopnea index (AHI) 5-14.9) and 20% with moderate to severe OSA (AHI ≥ 15). Male sex, higher age, and body mass index were significantly associated with OSA. However, there were no significant differences in other comorbidities, Long COVID symptom burden, quality of life measures (QoL), and objective cognitive function test results between groups. Additionally, multiple linear regression models demonstrated that neither AHI nor mean desaturation nadir were significant predictors of QoL or cognitive function. Although OSA is nearly twice as prevalent among our study participants compared to the general adult population of the US, it was not significantly associated with Long COVID symptoms, alteration of QoL, or objective cognitive dysfunction. However, 20% of patients were diagnosed with moderate to severe OSA, a clinically significant finding that warrants intervention to prevent irreversible cardiopulmonary complications.

studies.title: Randomized controlled trial of pirfenidone XR for patients with COVID-19 and exploration of effects on long-COVID incidence.
studies.journal: International journal of infectious diseases : IJID : official publication of the International Society for Infectious Diseases
studies.authors: M, Tamez-Torres Karla, Karina, Aguilar Laura, Alejandro, Díaz-Mejía Bruno, Maria de la Luz, Morales-Ortega et al.
studies.abstract: Evaluate safety and efficacy of extended-release pirfenidone (pirfenidone-XR), an anti-inflammatory and anti-fibrotic agent, as an early treatment for acute and long-term effects of COVID-19. This double-blinded, placebo-controlled trial randomized hospitalized and ambulatory COVID-19 patients in Mexico City 2:1 to pirfenidone-XR or placebo. The primary endpoint was recovery dynamics using a clinical severity 7-point ordinal scale; secondary and exploratory endpoints included long COVID incidence and safety. Planned enrollment was 801 patients to detect a 50% relative-risk reduction in key clinical outcomes. Between May 2020 and May 2021, 367 patients were enrolled, approximately 50% of the target. Evolving standards of care resulted in early termination and lower-than-anticipated event rates, limiting statistical power. Time-to-recovery analyses suggested improved dynamics with pirfenidone-XR: both groups had 53% full recovery by week 1; an additional 33% vs 21% achieved it during week 2, and 97% vs 90% by week 4. Long-term follow-up showed a numerically lower incidence of long COVID symptoms in 1, 2, 3 and 4 symptom domains in the pirfenidone-XR group: symptoms in ≥4 domains were reported in 5% vs 21% of hospitalized patients. There were no unexpected safety signals. Pirfenidone-XR was well tolerated and, although underpowered, demonstrated numerical trends of improved recovery and reduced long COVID risk. These findings support further investigation of pirfenidone-XR in patients infected with SARS-CoV-2 and similar post-infectious syndromes characterized by persistent immune activation and tissue remodeling.

studies.title: Mid-Term Outcomes for Lung Transplantation in for COVID-19 Respiratory Failure: An Analysis of the United Network for Organ Sharing Database.
studies.journal: The Journal of thoracic and cardiovascular surgery
studies.authors: Hassaballa, Aly Sherif, O'Neill, John W, Gregorio, Paulo H P, Mazur, Michael Zane et al.
studies.abstract: Lung transplantation is a feasible therapeutic option for irreversible lung injury caused by COVID-19, but comprehensive mid-term outcome data remain limited. This study evaluated outcomes after lung transplantation for COVID-19 acute respiratory distress syndrome (CARDS) and post-COVID pulmonary fibrosis (CPF) using a national registry. We performed a retrospective analysis of the United Network for Organ Sharing database from 2020 through 2024. Recipient characteristics, perioperative complications, and graft failure-free survival were analyzed in adult lung transplant recipients with a primary diagnosis of CARDS, CPF, or non-COVID restrictive lung disease (NCRLD). Inverse probability of treatment weighting (IPTW) and multivariate logistic regression were performed to adjust for potential confounders. During the study period, 256 transplants were performed for CARDS, 338 for CPF, and 8071 for NCRLD. Post-COVID-19 recipients were younger (54 vs. 64 years, p<0.001) and required a higher level of care preoperatively than NCRLD recipients. Posttransplant, post-COVID-19 recipients experienced higher rates of posttransplant ECMO (22.6% vs. 10.3%, p<0.001), ventilation >48 hours (67.5% vs. 43.3%, p<0.001), new dialysis (11.0% vs. 7.9%, p=0.012), and acute rejection (7.7% vs. 5.5%, p=0.026). Graft failure-free survival was equivalent throughout the first year posttransplant between the post-COVID-19 and NCRLD recipients and, after IPTW for age and other confounders, was equivalent for up to 3 years (Hochberg-adjusted p=0.118). Lung transplantation for post-COVID-19 lung damage yields comparable short-term and mid-term survival outcomes despite higher perioperative morbidity and resource utilization. Long-term studies are needed to assess chronic lung allograft dysfunction in this population.

studies.journal: Journal of occupational and environmental medicine
studies.authors: Garvey, Kathleen, Wambui, David, Vergara, Ximena
studies.abstract: We used California Health Interview Survey (CHIS) data to examine relationships between long COVID and financial hardship among California workers. We analyzed cross-sectional 2022-2023 CHIS adult survey data. Long COVID was defined as symptoms lasting two or more months among employed adults who previously had COVID-19. Logistic regression assessed associations between long COVID and financial hardship. Approximately 30% of workers who ever had COVID-19 reported long COVID symptoms in 2022 (30%; CI: 28.3-31.7%) and 2023 (29%; CI: 27.7-30.4%). Farming and Service occupation groups had the highest long COVID prevalence. Workers with long COVID had higher odds of experiencing financial hardship in both years. These findings underscore the need for COVID-19 workplace protections, accommodations for workers impacted by long COVID, and ongoing assessment of COVID-19's workforce impacts.

studies.title: Effectiveness of physical, psychological, and alternative interventions for post-COVID-19 condition: a systematic review.
studies.authors: Negm, Akram, Stolz, Maike, Krauth, Christian
studies.abstract: To evaluate supervised physical, psycho-logical, and alternative non-pharmacological interventions for improving patient-reported and objective functional outcomes in adults with post-COVID-19 condition. Systematic review of randomized controlled trials. PubMed, Web of Science Core Collection, APA PsycInfo, and Scopus were searched from 1 January 2020 to 29 January 2026. Eligible studies were supervised, face-to-face trials evaluating physical, psychological, or alternative non-pharmacological interventions against usual care, placebo/sham, or active comparators in adults with World Health Organization defined post-COVID-19 condition. Risk of bias was assessed using Cochrane RoB 2. Due to clinical and methodological heterogeneity, a narrative synthesis was performed. 27 trials (1,998 participants) were included and evaluated physical, psychological, and alternative therapies. Supervised cardiopulmonary rehabilitation and multimodal exercise consistently improved cardiorespiratory fitness and walking capacity. Cognitive-behavioural therapy and lifestyle adjustments significantly reduced fatigue and subjective concentration complaints. Findings for neuromodulation, complementary, and oxygen therapies were heterogeneous, often showing no benefit over placebo. Only 18.5% of trials had low risk of bias, limited by small samples, unblinding, and short follow-ups. Supervised physical rehabilitation and CBT show promising evidence for improving functional capacity and symptoms in post-COVID-19 condition. Larger trials with longer follow-up are needed to confirm effectiveness and inform clinical guidelines.

studies.title: Persistent Cognitive Vulnerability After COVID-19 in Older Adults: Longitudinal Clinical Trajectories and Multi-Cohort Transcriptomic Evidence.
studies.authors: Lara, Maximiliano Correa, Hernandez, Erika Martinez
studies.abstract: Older adults frequently experience persistent cognitive impairment after COVID-19, yet the mechanisms underlying impaired recovery and resilience remain poorly understood. Integrating longitudinal clinical trajectories with molecular signatures may clarify why cognitive function fails to recover in this population. We conducted a longitudinal study of adults aged ≥60 years hospitalized with COVID- 19, integrating comprehensive geriatric assessments across premorbid, morbid, and postmorbid states with transcriptomic analyses from three independent public cohorts (GSE152641, GSE196822, and GSE157103). Clinical resilience was classified as complete, partial, or absent across geriatric domains. Differential expression analyses, cross-cohort gene integration, and transcriptomic score analyses were performed to identify biological pathways associated with COVID-19 in older adults. Forty-nine older adults contributed 147 longitudinal observations. Cognitive performance (MoCA) declined significantly during acute COVID-19 compared with the premorbid state (p < 0.001) and remained persistently impaired during follow-up, with no improvement from the morbid state (p = 0.549), indicating absence of cognitive resilience. Depressive symptoms and mobility showed similar patterns of persistent impairment, whereas functional status and nutritional measures demonstrated partial recovery. Age was the only independent predictor of poorer outcomes across multiple geriatric domains (all p < 0.05). Transcriptomic analyses identified 66 genes consistently upregulated across all cohorts, including CDC6, RRM2, CDCA2, DTL, MCM10, and CLSPN. The most reproducible molecular finding was activation of interferon-responsive pathways. The Interferon Response Score was significantly elevated in the pooled meta-analysis (Hedges' g = 1.00, 95% CI 0.14-1.87, p = 0.022), whereas Neuroinflammation and Synaptic Function scores were not significantly altered. Persistent cognitive impairment after COVID-19 was accompanied by a reproducible interferon-associated transcriptional signature across independent cohorts of older adults. The absence of recovery in cognition, together with sustained activation of interferon-responsive pathways, suggests that aging-related immune dysregulation may contribute to impaired resilience following COVID-19. In contrast, broader neuroinflammatory and synaptic transcriptional signatures showed limited reproducibility, highlighting interferon signaling as the most consistent biological correlate of post-COVID vulnerability. COVID-19 in older adults induces a state of persistent vulnerability characterized by incomplete cognitive recovery and sustained activation of interferon-associated transcriptional programs. The dominant influence of age and the absence of both clinical and molecular resilience suggest that recovery is constrained by aging-related biological processes. These findings identify interferon signaling as a potential therapeutic target for improving long-term outcomes in older COVID-19 survivors.

studies.title: Simultaneous determination of serotonin and its precursor tryptophan in small volumes of human serum using HPLC-ECD.
studies.authors: Licht, Dorothee, Duscha, Alexander, Hegelmaier, Tobias, Desel, Christiane et al.
studies.abstract: Serotonin (5-HT) is not only a key neurotransmitter in the brain but also plays an important role in peripheral tissues e.g. in the gastrointestinal (GI) tract. The multitude of processes in which 5-HT is involved explains why recent studies have linked altered 5-HT levels to Long Covid (LC) and fatigue. LC is a post-viral syndrome which can occur after a SARS-CoV-2 infection with various symptoms, amongst others including fatigue. We present an optimized bioanalytical HPLC method with electrochemical detection (ECD) for the simultaneous detection of 5-HT and its precursor tryptophan (W) in small volumes of human serum. We validated the method with a calibration curve better representing concentrations expected in human serum; with the possibility to concurrently measure W and low 5-HT concentrations. Sample comparability and standardization were improved through an adapted sample preparation, reducing transfer errors and increasing recovery of the internal standard (IS). The simple preparation involved only two steps: protein precipitation and sample dilution. After a brief series of validation measurements of the optimized method, it was applied to human serum from an observational study cohort.•Easy-to-use method for detecting 5-HT and W in human serum without the need for expensive buffer ingredients or pre-filter units.•Enables measurement of triplicates with less than 100 µL serum.

studies.title: Resurgence of Sexually Transmitted Hepatitis C Virus Infection in Men Who Have Sex With Men Living With HIV.
studies.authors: Lee, Shui-Shan, Chan, Denise Pui-Chung, Wong, Bonnie Chun-Kwan, Cheung, Danny King Fai et al.
studies.abstract: In 2023-2025, HCV transmission in men who have sex with men (MSM) living with HIV in Hong Kong resurged. This study aims to assess the epidemiologic patterns between 2011 and 2025. Among 288 MSM with sexually acquired HCV infection, 73% were diagnosed at least 12 months after HIV diagnosis, and 98% had ever achieved HIV viral load suppression. Comparing with Period 1 (2015-2022) featuring a large HCV genotype 3a cluster (89 diagnoses) and a few smaller HCV genotype 1a clusters (size of 2 to 13), Period 2 (2023-2025) was dominated by two HCV genotype 1a clusters (7 and 16 new diagnoses). Transmission of genotype 3a viruses subsided in Period 2, with only 3 new diagnoses. Comparing with Period 1, a higher proportion of MSM with HCV diagnoses in Period 2 self-reported sexualised injecting drug use (OR = 3.82, 95% CI 1.59-9.20) and HCV direct-acting antivirals therapy (no treatment as reference group, OR = 3.72, 95%CI 1.82-7.60). The epidemic rebound by a different HCV genotype was likely contributed by increased engagement in chemsex and post-COVID-19 population mobility.

studies.title: Potential association between dementia polygenic risk scores and subjective cognitive burden in a post-COVID cohort: a hypothesis-generating study.
studies.authors: Nasif, Aleemah, Sunil, Punya, Das, Ranajit
studies.abstract: Coronavirus disease 2019 (COVID-19) may be associated with persistent subjective cognitive complaints, including difficulties with attention, memory, and executive function, in some individuals with post-acute sequelae of SARS-CoV-2 infection (PASC, "long COVID"). Inter-individual variability raises the possibility that host genetic factors contribute to susceptibility. This study explored the relationship between dementia-related polygenic risk scores (PRS) and subjective cognitive burden after COVID-19. Genome-wide genotype data from 60 individuals with a history of COVID-19 were merged with 915 South Asian population reference samples (total COVID-19-affected individuals aged 18-52 years showed a modest rightward shift in dementia-related PRS compared with population reference samples, with substantial overlap between groups (mean standardized PRS 0.24 vs. - 0.01; Mann-Whitney U = 29,504.5, This hypothesis-generating study identified a possible relationship between dementia-related genetic liability and subjective cognitive burden after COVID-19. The PRS group comparison was descriptive and should not be interpreted as evidence of increased dementia risk. The phenotype-genotype finding is severely limited by the small subgroup, possible selection bias, non-validated subjective assessment, lack of multivariable adjustment, and cross-sectional design. Validation in larger, ancestry-matched, longitudinal cohorts is required.

studies.title: [Intersection of gender, working conditions, and caregiving burden in post-COVID-19 syndrome: A cross-sectional mixed-methods study among healthcare workers].
studies.authors: Antonietti, Laura, Straw, Cecilia, Riveiro, Manuel, Martínez, María José et al.
studies.abstract: Post-COVID-19 syndrome (PCS) among healthcare personnel impacts quality of life and work performance negatively, and is associated with gender and work conditions. The study aimed to characterize PCS in healthcare personnel and explore their perceptions regarding gender conditions, work, and caregiving burden. Between May and October 2023, a cross-sectional mixed-methods study was conducted in health professionals with a history of COVID-19 who worked in Buenos Aires City and Buenos Aires Province. PCS was defined as the persistence of symptoms for more than one month. Using nonprobability snowball sampling strategy, an anonymous survey was conducted on clinical, sociodemographic, occupational, gender, and caregiving variables, along with individual and group interviews. The information was analyzed according to the Ecological and Social Framework. A total of 444 surveys and 22 interviews were analyzed. The overall prevalence of PCS was 57%, with a higher frequency and number of symptoms in women, a finding that remained consistent when disaggregated by profession. In the multivariate analysis, female gender, non-permanent employment, the number of COVID-19 episodes, and the perception of a heavier domestic workload were associated with a higher likelihood of PCS. The qualitative component revealed an unequal distribution of caregiving responsibilities, a greater mental burden on women, work overload, and limited institutional support. The findings suggest that clinical experience of PCS among healthcare workers is situated at the intersection of gender, work, and caregiving distribution. This approach can guide future research and generate hypotheses for preventive and healthcare-worker support policies in the face of future emergencies. Introducción: El síndrome post-COVID-19 (SPC) en personal de salud impacta en peor calidad de vida y menor desempeño laboral, y se asocia con condiciones de género y trabajo. El estudio buscó caracterizar el SPC en profesionales de salud y explorar sus percepciones respecto de condiciones de género, trabajo y carga de cuidado. Materiales y métodos: Entre mayo y octubre de 2023 se realizó un estudio transversal de métodos mixtos en profesionales de salud con antecedente de COVID-19 que trabajaban en Ciudad y Provincia de Buenos Aires. Se consideró SPC la persistencia de síntomas mayor a un mes. Mediante muestreo no probabilístico, se realizó una encuesta anónima sobre variables clínicas, sociodemográficas, laborales de género y cuidados, y entrevistas individuales y grupales. La información se analizó según el Modelo Ecológico y Social. Resultados: Se analizaron 444 encuestas y 22 entrevistas. La prevalencia global de SPC fue 57%, con mayor frecuencia y número de síntomas en mujeres, que se mantuvo al desagregar por profesión. En el análisis multivariado, el género femenino, la contratación no permanente, la cantidad de episodios de COVID-19 y la percepción de mayor carga de trabajo doméstico se asociaron con mayor probabilidad de SPC. El componente cualitativo mostró distribución desigual del cuidado, mayor carga mental en mujeres, sobrecarga laboral y escasa contención institucional. Conclusión: Los hallazgos sugieren que el SPC en personal de salud se inscribe en la intersección entre género, trabajo y organización del cuidado. Este enfoque puede orientar futuras investigaciones y generar hipótesis para políticas preventivas y de cuidado ante futuras emergencias.

studies.title: [An insight into the long/post COVID care situation in Germany-a rapid scoping review].
studies.authors: Ebster, Marlene, Gscheidle, Sonja, Lange, Saskia, Weijburg, Thomas et al.
studies.abstract: Long/post COVID and related conditions such as myalgic encephalomyelitis/chronic fatigue syndrome, postural orthostatic tachycardia syndrome and post-vaccination syndrome are associated with persistent functional impairments and are met with care structures in Germany that are difficult to navigate. The rapid scoping review offers an insight into care structures, capacities, access, care pathways and gaps in care for these patient groups in the German healthcare system. It also takes into account patient and care provider perspectives. The study follows the recommendations of the Joanna Briggs Institute and the PRISMA ScR checklist for conducting (rapid) scoping reviews. A MEDLINE search was conducted from 2020 onwards with predefined inclusion and exclusion criteria for evidence sources related to care in Germany. 44 evidence sources were included. General practitioners and paediatricians act as the first point of contact. Specialised outpatient clinics and rehabilitation facilities take on complex diagnostics and patient treatment. Care networks are rare. Navigating the healthcare system is characterised by information gaps, unclear responsibilities and long waiting times, so that those affected often organise their own care. Some report stigmatisation, misdiagnoses and stressful activation recommendations despite the risk of post exertional malaise. Care is unevenly accessible, poorly coordinated and only limitedly evidence based. Shared knowledge and case databases, training, better diagnostic tools and robust efficacy studies are needed to improve access, management and safety of long/post COVID care. HINTERGRUND: Long/Post COVID und verwandte Krankheitsbilder wie Myalgische Enzephalomyelitis/Chronisches Fatigue Syndrom, Posturales Orthostatisches Tachykardiesyndrom (POTS) und Postvakzinierungssyndrom gehen mit anhaltenden Funktionseinschränkungen einher und treffen auf schwer überschaubare Versorgungsstrukturen. ZIEL: Der Rapid Scoping Review bietet einen Einblick in Versorgungsstrukturen, Kapazitäten, Zugänge und Versorgungslücken für diese Patientengruppen im deutschen Gesundheitssystem. Dabei werden auch die Perspektiven von Leistungserbringenden und Betroffenen berücksichtigt. Die Arbeit folgt den Empfehlungen des Joanna Briggs Institute und der PRISMA-ScR-Checkliste zur Durchführung von (Rapid) Scoping Reviews. Es erfolgte eine MEDLINE-Suche ab 2020 mit vordefinierten Ein- und Ausschlusskriterien für Evidenzquellen mit Bezug zur Versorgung in Deutschland. Es wurden 44 Quellen eingeschlossen. Haus- und kinderärztliche Praxen fungieren als erste Anlaufstelle. Spezialisierte Ambulanzen und Rehabilitationseinrichtungen übernehmen komplexe Diagnostik und Patientenbehandlung. Versorgungsnetzwerke sind selten. Die Navigation von Betroffenen durch das Gesundheitswesen ist von Informationslücken, unklaren Zuständigkeiten und langen Wartezeiten geprägt, sodass diese ihre Versorgung häufig selbst organisieren. Betroffene berichten teilweise von Stigmatisierung, Fehldiagnosen und belastenden Aktivierungsempfehlungen trotz des Risikos einer Post-Exertionellen Malaise. Die Versorgung ist ungleich zugänglich, wenig koordiniert und nur begrenzt evidenzbasiert. Gemeinsame Wissens- und Falldatenbanken, Fortbildungen, bessere diagnostische Instrumente und robuste Wirksamkeitsstudien sind erforderlich, um Zugang, Steuerung und Sicherheit der Long/Post COVID-Versorgung zu verbessern.

studies.title: Dysregulated complement activation in COVID-19: The Role of Soluble Complement Inhibitors.
studies.authors: van der Meulen, Stef, Wang, Haiyu, Nugteren, Saskia, Ponchel, Frederique et al.
studies.abstract: In viral infections, complement activation can contribute to viral clearance, but excessive activation, as observed in severe COVID-19, may drive immunopathology. While much is known about complement-activating factors in COVID-19, insight into the role of endogenous complement inhibitors remains limited. We performed a longitudinal analysis within the BEAT-COVID cohort, comprising hospitalized patients with SARS-CoV-2 infection admitted to the intensive care unit (ICU) or ward, and age-matched healthy controls. Serum levels of the complement activation marker soluble membrane attack complex (sC5b-9) and soluble inhibitors C1-Inhibitor (C1-INH), C4b-Binding Protein (C4BP), Factor H, and Factor I were measured by ELISA. In vitro endothelial complement sensitivity was assessed by flow cytometry. Soluble inhibitors were also measured in a cohort of patients with long COVID. Patients admitted to the ICU showed elevated sC5b-9 levels compared to patients admitted to the ward and controls, correlating with disease severity, length of hospitalization, and need for mechanical ventilation, but not mortality. Unexpectedly, levels of all soluble complement inhibitors were elevated, particularly in patients admitted to the ICU. Factor H levels positively correlated with sC5b-9. Endothelial cells pre-incubated with serum from patients admitted to the ICU became more susceptible to complement attack. In patients with long COVID, Factor H and C4BP levels remained elevated compared to pre-pandemic healthy controls. Severe COVID-19 is characterized by extensive complement activation despite elevated circulating inhibitor levels, suggesting impaired local complement regulation at the cell surface, potentially amplified by overwhelming systemic activation, rather than inhibitor deficiency.

studies.title: Potential Physiological Convergence Between GLP-1 Receptor Signaling and Hepatocyte TAZ in Metabolic Liver Disease: From Metabolic Homeostasis to Fibrotic Remodeling.
studies.authors: Gholam, Mohammed F
studies.abstract: Metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD) progresses when nutrient excess, insulin resistance, adipose dysfunction, and hepatocellular stress overwhelm hepatic adaptation. Glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonists (GLP-1RAs) improve weight, glycemic control, and steatohepatitis, and semaglutide has demonstrated histological improvement in metabolic dysfunction-associated steatohepatitis (MASH). In parallel, the transcriptional coactivator with PDZ-binding motif (TAZ; WWTR1) has emerged as a nutrient-, cholesterol-, and mechanics-responsive regulator linking stressed hepatocytes to inflammation and fibrogenesis through Hippo-YAP/TAZ signaling and Indian hedgehog. This narrative review integrates incretin physiology with cell-specific TAZ biology across the gut-brain-axis, adipose tissue, pancreatic islets, liver sinusoidal endothelial cells, hepatocytes, immune cells, and hepatic stellate cells. Recent evidence that semaglutide can signal through intrahepatic sinusoidal endothelial GLP-1 receptors provides a weight-loss-independent route to reduced hepatic inflammation and fibrosis; however, it does not establish that TAZ is a downstream mediator. The evidence therefore supports a multilevel convergence model in which GLP-1RAs lower metabolic and inflammatory inputs that favor TAZ activation, while direct GLP-1RA-to-TAZ signaling remains a testable hypothesis. Receptor-validated, cell-specific, weight-controlled, and longitudinal human studies are needed to distinguish mediation from parallel response and to determine whether TAZ-pathway biomarkers can guide mechanism-based therapy.
